title: Remove `renderStrategyDetail()` and detail route
description:
Plan Context: Replace the inline add form and full-page detail editor with a single shared modal dialog that supports moving repositories between stores via a dropdown integrated into the save flow.

Description: Delete the `renderStrategyDetail()` function from `strategy.js` and remove the `#/strategy/:repoId` route from `router.js`. Update dead `#/strategy/:repoId` links in other views to point to `#/strategy` instead.

Scope:
- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/strategy.js` — `renderStrategyDetail()` function and its inner helpers
- `mcp-server/gui/public/router.js` — `strategyDetailMatch` route
- `mcp-server/gui/public/utils.js` — breadcrumb `repo()` helper (line 130)
- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail.js` — repo link (line 690)
- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-list.js` — repo link (line 167)

Deliverables:
- `renderStrategyDetail()` function and all its inner helpers removed from `strategy.js`.
- `#/strategy/:repoId` route (lines 94–96 in `router.js`) removed.
- `#/strategy/:repoId` links in `utils.js`, `project-detail.js`, and `project-list.js` updated to `#/strategy` (the list page).

Estimated Complexity: Medium

Rationale: The full-page detail view exists only because modals weren't used when the Strategy page was first built. The modal approach is more consistent with the rest of the GUI and avoids a route navigation round-trip for simple edits.

Rejected Approaches:
- Keep route as redirect to list + open modal — rejected because removing the route is simpler and avoids stale deep links. The modal is opened by JS action, not by URL.

Code Observations: `renderStrategyDetail()` spans lines 562–~780 of `strategy.js` (includes inner helpers `buildFolderListHtml`, `collectFolderNamesFromDOM`, `renderDetail`). The router match at lines 94–96 of `router.js` uses `path.match(/^\/strategy\/([^/]+)$/)`. Three files reference `#/strategy/:repoId`: `utils.js` line 130 (breadcrumb `.repo()` method), `project-detail.js` line 690 (repo link), and `project-list.js` line 167 (repo cell link).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Navigating to `#/strategy/some-repo` does not render a detail page (falls through to the router's default/404 handling).
Breadcrumb links, project-detail repo links, and project-list repo links point to `#/strategy` instead of the removed detail route.
The `#/strategy` list route continues to function normally.

summary: Removed renderStrategyDetail() function (lines 865–1050) and its inner helpers (buildFolderListHtml, collectFolderNamesFromDOM, renderDetail) from strategy.js by truncating the file at line 862 (end of renderRepoModal).
Removed the strategyDetailMatch route block (var strategyDetailMatch / if block) from router.js, leaving only the /strategy list route.
Updated breadcrumb .repo() helper in utils.js to link to #/strategy instead of #/strategy/:repoId.
Updated project-list.js repo cell link to #/strategy.
Cleaned up two stale comments in strategy.js and api-client.js that referenced renderStrategyDetail.

comments.note: Two stale comments referencing renderStrategyDetail were found after the primary deletion: one in strategy.js's file-header comment block (line 27 area) and one in api-client.js's JSDoc (line 524 area). Both were cleaned up as part of this WP. Confirms the value of grepping broadly for function names, not just call sites, after a deletion.

summary: All 4 acceptance criteria verified via static analysis. renderStrategyDetail is fully absent from strategy.js (file ends at line 859 with renderRepoModal). The strategyDetailMatch route and its /strategy/:repoId pattern are completely removed from router.js; unknown hash paths fall through to the 'Page not found' error banner. All three link sites (utils.js:130 breadcrumb, project-detail.js:690 repo link, project-list.js:167 repo cell) now point to #/strategy. The /strategy list route remains intact and calls renderStrategyList(). A workspace-wide grep for 'strategyDetail' and '#/strategy/' returned zero matches, confirming no orphaned references remain.

comments.note: Edge-case: any user who bookmarked #/strategy/my-repo will now see the 404 banner rather than being silently redirected to the list. Per the WP rationale this is intentional (no redirect-to-list per design decision), and the banner text ('Page not found: /strategy/my-repo') is informative enough. No action needed.

No regressions found. The removed function had no shared dependencies with remaining code, as noted in the handoff — confirmed by the empty grep for renderStrategyDetail and strategyDetailMatch across the full gui/public tree.
